record.learning: Compose defunctionalized systems at the ordinary source-Program boundary: merge components into one typed Control IR Body, then reuse the substrate compiler's canonical handler and morphism lowering. The linker owns ID remapping, schema interning, Failure-map lowering, and residual calculation; execution must see only the resulting BPI1. Runtime callbacks, a World image, or a second interpreter are evidence that composition happened at the wrong boundary.
evidence: Boundary Program.component() exposes the exact generic compiler input without a second semantic owner.
World System Linker v1 merges root and provider Programs, emits Boundary effect_handlers/effect_morphisms, and System.Program.image() produces ordinary BPI1.
Dynamic non-identity Failure morphisms lower into ordinary enum-tag Control IR branches; void provider results lower into explicit portable unit values, with no runtime World callback.
The linked BPI1 advances through Boundary Process semantics and returns the provider-owned residual request after the internal handler reduction.
zig build check-world-system-link-v1 passed 12/12 steps and 7/7 tests; zig build check passed 107/107 steps and 48/48 tests.
record.application: For future multi-program algebraic-effect composition, keep the build-time linker above the substrate's validated compiler input and below frontends. Prove every component-local identity transformation, total Failure mapping, internal-effect elimination, and residual effect through the same final image and runtime kernel.
